findings.review_scope: Registered-source content review of arXiv:2211.11400v3, with margin stamp 21 December 2023 and title-page date 22 December 2023, by Lasse Fischer, Marta Bofill Roig and Werner Brannath. The PDF has 21 pages. Main text ends on physical page 16. Only the Appendix heading on page 17 was inspected; no appendix body was read. Fresh text evidence covers all 16 main-paper pages. Original theorem formulas, definitions and boundary pages were inspected visually.
findings.inventory: Exactly four actual Theorem headings occur: 3.2 on page 3, 3.5 on page 4, 3.9 on page 6 and 4.2 on page 8. All complete statements match the rendered PDF. Bold-heading enumeration distinguishes the regular-font Theorem 3.5 reference on page 5. Lemmas, Propositions, Corollaries, Remarks and appendix results are excluded.
original_statements: Theorem 3.2 retains the arbitrary family of level-alpha intersection tests and its strong-FWER conclusion separately from the additional online and predictable-family premises of the online-procedure conclusion. The minimum ranges over all subsets containing i, and the closing naming sentence is retained.

Theorem 3.5 preserves the maximum construction, its predictable/online/level-alpha conclusion and the exact equality of decision sequences. It assumes no admissibility property. The Section 3 convention phi_empty=0 is stored separately rather than inserted into its quotation.

Theorem 3.9 preserves all four family properties, the base set {1}, the recursion using non-rejected intersection tests, the i>=2 qualifier and both equivalent procedures, including all i in the shortcut definition.

Theorem 4.2 preserves threshold-family predictability, the explicit equation (3) reference, separately assumed level and consonance, the recursion using strict p_j>alpha_j^{I_j}, and all three decision-equivalent procedures. The threshold decision retains non-strict p_i<=alpha_i^{I_i}.
source_passages: All 13 source entries and six auxiliary passages were checked. The experiment, model laws, fixed hypothesis subsets, almost-sure convention and increasing filtration match pages 2-3. Definition 2.1 requires current-time measurable binary decisions. Strong all-time FWER, true-null indices, the increasing rejection count and its limit match equation (1) and the accompanying prose.

Page 3 supplies possibly infinite intersection hypotheses and binary tests, phi_empty=0, measurability at F_sup(I) with F_infinity=A, the marginal level-alpha bound and Definition 3.1. The latter permits only future extensions of a finite prefix intersection; it does not impose arbitrary-superset monotonicity.

The closure operation is an inline theorem excerpt, and consonance (2) on page 4 is a distinct definition with a witnessing index and all containing sub-intersections. Neither is rewritten as an assumption nor conflated with the other.

Page 7 supplies adapted marginally valid p-values, individual thresholds in [0,1), current-information online alpha-adjustments, the sub-adjustment construction and equation (3), and Definition 4.1. Existing thresholds must remain equal under future extensions. This is different from rejection persistence, as explicitly explained after that definition.

The general-versus-strict information growth, default strong-control convention, finite-prefix lemma, optional conditional-validity construction, independent-p-value example and distinction between the two predictability notions match their source passages. Later Alpha-Spending, Online-Graph and ADDIS applications are not required to state these four theorems.
findings.dependency_review: All 27 direct uses, all 13 reach sets, and all 35 related connections were reviewed. The experiment, online decisions, intersection hypotheses, online intersection tests, level condition and closure reach all four theorems. Rejection-persistence predictability reaches only 3.2, 3.5 and 3.9; it is a consequence, rather than an independently named premise, in 4.2. Consonance reaches 3.9 and 4.2. Strong FWER reaches 3.2 and 3.5. The four p-value/threshold entries reach only 4.2. The D12 -> D5 correction is based on an explicit source term, not on a proof that one assumption implies another.
findings.names_and_highlights: Every source entry retains natural-language keywords and its original heading or neutral passage heading. All highlight selectors identify the original passage or a related theorem occurrence. Definitions 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 remain distinct; the source experiment is a source passage and the closure is a theorem excerpt. No symbol list replaces a readable name, and no umbrella definition is invented.
findings.source_limitations: All 18 existing notes were reviewed. They preserve uncountable-minimum measurability and simultaneous-version limitations; empty-index conventions; distinctions between online measurability, level control and two predictability properties; current-time rather than necessarily previous-time thresholds; marginal versus conditional validity; adaptive finite-subset evaluation; decision equality versus distributional equality; strong infinite-horizon FWER; fixed hypothesis subsets; the precise consonance witness; unspecified computational costs; strict versus non-strict decision comparisons; the absence of admissibility and application-specific requirements; and the two printed source dates. Source fidelity does not certify correctness of the printed results.

This adds one indirect Theorem 4.2 connection, changing 34 to 35 related connections while preserving 27 direct uses, all original theorem statements and all source quotations.
